court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Ghaziabad in Matrimonial Case No.219 of 2025
case_name: Mukesh Arora vs Smt Neha Arora
facts_of_case: Petitioner was married to respondent according to Hindu rites and customs on 23.08.2004. A matrimonial dispute arose between the parties and they started living separately from 26.06.2020. A divorce petition was moved on 21.01.2025 under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: In determining whether a provision is mandatory or directory, language alone is not always decisive.
legal_principles.held: The court has to have regard to the context, subject-matter and object of the provision.
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — for understanding the scope of Section 13B

legal_principles.principle: The court should not be powerless in enabling parties to have a better option when there are no chances of reunion and there are chances of fresh rehabilitation.
legal_principles.held: Though every effort has to be made to save a marriage, if there are no chances of reunion and there are chances of fresh rehabilitation, the Court should not be powerless in enabling the parties to have a better option.
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — for understanding the purpose of Section 13B

outcome.final_order: The application for waiving off cooling period has been allowed.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: representing clients in Family Court matters
